q1: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2: WITH ALT AS ( SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ) SELECT MAX(NUM) NUM FROM ALT
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2_prompt_sql: WITH ALT AS ( SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ) SELECT MAX(NUM) NUM FROM ALT
explanation: Both Q1 and Q2 aim to find the maximum of distinct numbers in the MYNUMBERS table. They both use GROUP BY with HAVING COUNT = 1 to retrieve distinct values and then apply MAX on the result. The syntax differences (GROUP BY NUM vs GROUP BY 1) do not affect the outcome since the column being grouped is the only column in the table.
